Validations.Reason: The chapter explicitly depicts Elias and Kaelen abandoning the temple due to structural instability (cracks in stone) and the overwhelming nature of the entity. They escape through a secret lower passage (the altar shaft). The text confirms they were driven out by the creature after fighting off smaller channel creatures in the drainage system, matching the proposed summary.

The chapter clarifies that the barrier functions as a trap designed to draw corruption in and consume it ('This was not simply a fortress... It was a trap built to draw corruption in and consume it'). It also reveals that smaller creatures inhabit the drainage channels and are awakened by Kaelen's blood, confirming the broader infestation described in the proposed change.

The chapter confirms the barrier is actively consuming the Blight to strengthen itself ('The barrier drank the Blight', 'The light brightened until Elias could no longer look directly at it'). It reveals the temple was built around a pre-existing containment system involving springs and lower passages, and provides a map showing six smaller shrines and a web of channels beneath the city, validating the proposed developments.
